subject: Psychology
central_question: How do sensory systems register stimulation, attention select information and perception organise it into a meaningful world?
in_scope_units: Sensation, attention and perception in knowing the world.
External and internal stimuli and seven sensory systems.
Sense modalities, psychophysics, absolute and difference thresholds.
Attention: alertness, concentration, search, focus and fringe.
Selective attention, determinants and filter theories.
Divided and sustained attention, vigilance and span.
Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder as presented in the chapter.
The perceiver: motivation, expectation, cognitive style and culture.
Space, depth and distance through monocular and binocular cues.
banned_topics: Detailed anatomy of sensory organs beyond the chapter’s functional account.
Clinical treatment recommendations for attention disorders beyond the textbook box.

known_pitfalls.correction: Sensation registers stimulation; perception recognises and constructs meaning.

known_pitfalls.claim: Absolute threshold is fixed for everyone.
known_pitfalls.correction: It varies across people and situations and is estimated over trials.

known_pitfalls.claim: Divided attention gives equal attention to two new difficult tasks.
known_pitfalls.correction: It works best when activities are highly practised and relatively automatic.
Learning, memory, motivation, expectation and culture contribute to construction.
Some are universal or permanent while others vary personally and culturally.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Review Question 1 on sensory limits.
NCERT Review Question 3 on selective and sustained attention.
NCERT Review Question 4 on Gestalt organisation.
NCERT Review Question 6 on depth cues.
NCERT Review Question 8 on socio-cultural influences.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter ends with Review Questions 1–8 and two Project Ideas.
